trigger: The terminal-boundary validator classifies bracketed-paste corruption, partial paste, unexpected literal control markers, or inconsistent command-not-found output.

steps.action: Do not authenticate, clone, reinstall or mutate repository state while the command-delivery boundary is ambiguous.
Keep the existing tmux session alive and preserve any already-written evidence logs.
Remove credentials, OAuth device codes, tokens and private key material from any diagnostic capture.
Manually type a short command-resolution probe such as gh --version instead of pasting the failed long command.
If the typed probe passes, repair or bypass the paste/input source rather than reinstalling the executable.
Resume at the first unproved downstream step only after the exact command boundary passes.
If a manually typed probe also fails, collect command -v, PATH and package-state evidence and hand off without destructive cleanup.

rollback: No rollback is needed for a read-only input diagnosis; any package mutation attempted outside this workflow must be handled by its owning package-management step.
proofCeiling: Recovery of the shell command-delivery boundary only.
